intent: Switch to the previous page of a paged result set through state, with a chevron and a short label.
typical_uses: The previous button at the start of the page row, disabled at the first page
Half of a previous/next pair with no page numbers

dont_use_when.situation: A button to one numbered page
A button to the next page
A link to the previous page, where each page has its own URL

invariants.text: The button renders a left chevron before the label and ignores children. With the default `text` its accessible name is "Go to previous page", set ahead of the consumer's props. A custom `text` is the name instead, since the visible label is hidden below 640px and the chevron is decorative; an empty or blank `text`, the icon-only form, keeps "Go to previous page". An `aria-label` passed to it replaces either.
The visible label is hidden below a 640px viewport width (pagination.module.css `.previousNextText`), so a narrow viewport shows the chevron alone.
The chevron is mirrored under a right-to-left direction (pagination.module.css `.chevron:dir(rtl)`), so it keeps pointing toward the previous pages whatever the reading direction.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass an `aria-label` that leaves out the words of a custom `text`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave `aria-label` off, so the name follows `text`; when you do override it, keep the visible words in it, or a voice-control user who says what is on screen cannot press the button

anti_patterns.dont: Disable a Previous or Next button that keyboard users page with, and leave `focusableWhenDisabled` off
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `focusableWhenDisabled` along with `disabled`: a button that becomes natively disabled while it holds focus loses it to the page, so the next Tab starts over from the top of the document

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Go to previous page' }) finds the button with the default `text`, whose visible label is "Previous" beside an svg, that a custom `text` "Forward" is the name instead, that an `aria-label` passed to it wins over either, and that an empty or blank `text` keeps "Go to previous page". It also asserts that a disabled one matches `:disabled` and fires no click, and that with `focusableWhenDisabled` it takes focus, reports aria-disabled and carries no native `disabled`. jsdom focuses anything with a tabindex, which Base UI's Button always sets, so the suite cannot show a natively disabled button refusing focus; that rests on the browser's own handling of `disabled`

rtl.by: pagination.module.css mirrors the chevron with `.chevron:dir(rtl)` and pagination.test.tsx pins that rule, but jsdom has no layout and does not resolve `:dir()`, so no suite renders the button right-to-left

unexposed_parts.reason: pagination.tsx renders a ChevronLeftIcon inside the button; it is not exported as a component of its own and cannot be replaced.
pagination.tsx renders `text` in a span with the stylesheet's previousNextText class; it is not exported, and `text` is the only control over it.

good.title: Disabled at the first page, keeping the focus a keyboard user has on it
A custom label, which is also the accessible name

bad.title: A label given as children
bad.why: The button renders fixed content and ignores children; the visible label is set through `text`.
